correctness.rationale: The full complex integral H3 rank B_n and vanishing in other degrees is attributed to Green. Direct group-generation shows its fundamental group vanishes: any two-coordinate generator edge reduces to coordinate basis flips, and commutator squares are triangulated. The vertex link is the clique complex of J(n,2), decomposed into n star simplices plus triangle cells; it has homotopy type the 2-skeleton of an (n-1)-simplex and reduced H2 rank C(n-1,3). An integral octahedral H2 basis from four-coordinate sets containing a reference coordinate is coned by the corresponding surviving even four-set, so the link-to-deletion map is zero. Mayer–Vietoris gives a split primitive H3 injection with cokernel Z^C(n-1,3) and no remaining homology. Connected link, van Kampen, and a high-dimensional star-clique collapse yield a two-connected three-dimensional complex, hence by Hurewicz and homology Whitehead an integral wedge of 3-spheres. Independently enumerated the full/punctured complexes n=4,5,6, matching exact mod2 reduced Betti counts 1/0,9/5,49/39. Those finite mod2 checks do not prove all-n integral homotopy.

final_claim: For every n>=4 and every even-parity vertex v, deleting v before taking the clique complex of the distance-two halved cube produces a wedge of B_n-C(n-1,3) three-spheres, with an integral primitive split inclusion into the undeleted wedge of B_n three-spheres.
limitations: Only one deleted even-parity vertex, inclusive Hamming radius two, no equivariant finer classification.
